response.sql: WITH rental_totals AS (SELECT r.rental_id, i.store_id, SUM(p.amount) AS payment_total FROM payment p JOIN rental r ON r.rental_id = p.rental_id JOIN inventory i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id GROUP BY r.rental_id, i.store_id), benchmark AS (SELECT AVG(payment_total) AS avg_payment_total FROM rental_totals) SELECT rt.store_id, SUM(rt.payment_total) AS combined_payment_total, AVG(rt.payment_total - b.avg_payment_total) AS average_amount_above_average FROM rental_totals rt CROSS JOIN benchmark b WHERE rt.payment_total > b.avg_payment_total GROUP BY rt.store_id ORDER BY rt.store_id

assumptions.assumption: The benchmark is the average payment total per paid rental across all stores. Rentals with no linked payments have no total and are excluded.

alternatives.interpretation: Compare each rental with the average payment total for paid rentals at its own store.
alternatives.sql: WITH rental_totals AS (SELECT r.rental_id, i.store_id, SUM(p.amount) AS payment_total FROM payment p JOIN rental r ON r.rental_id = p.rental_id JOIN inventory i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id GROUP BY r.rental_id, i.store_id), store_benchmarks AS (SELECT store_id, AVG(payment_total) AS avg_payment_total FROM rental_totals GROUP BY store_id) SELECT rt.store_id, SUM(rt.payment_total) AS combined_payment_total, AVG(rt.payment_total - sb.avg_payment_total) AS average_amount_above_average FROM rental_totals rt JOIN store_benchmarks sb ON sb.store_id = rt.store_id WHERE rt.payment_total > sb.avg_payment_total GROUP BY rt.store_id ORDER BY rt.store_id
